hook: Photo apps rotate, flip, stretch and slant pictures. Each of those moves sends every point of the image to a new point by the same rule, keeps the center fixed and keeps straight lines straight. Every such move is a matrix, and the matrix can be read straight off a picture of where the square goes.

figure.caption: The matrix $\left[ \begin{matrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{matrix} \right]$ sends $\left\langle 1, 0 \right\rangle$ to its first column, $\left\langle 1, 0 \right\rangle$, and $\left\langle 0, 1 \right\rangle$ to its second column, $\left\langle 1, 2 \right\rangle$. The unit square becomes a parallelogram of area $2$, the determinant.

chain.cause: $L(\left\langle x, y \right\rangle) = \left\langle ax + by, cx + dy \right\rangle$
chain.effect: $L$ is multiplication by the matrix $\left[ \begin{matrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{matrix} \right]$, with the input written as a column
you get the first and second columns of the matrix

chain.cause: Every point moves by the same matrix
chain.effect: the origin stays put, lines stay lines and the grid becomes a grid of parallelograms

chain.cause: Take the determinant of the matrix
chain.effect: its absolute value is the factor by which every area is multiplied; a negative sign means the picture is flipped

ideas: A linear transformation of the plane has the form $L(\left\langle x, y \right\rangle) = \left\langle ax + by, cx + dy \right\rangle$: multiplication by $\left[ \begin{matrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{matrix} \right]$.
The columns of the matrix are $L(\left\langle 1, 0 \right\rangle)$ and $L(\left\langle 0, 1 \right\rangle)$, so a picture of where the unit square goes gives the matrix.

Rotation by $\theta$ counterclockwise: $\left[ \begin{matrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{matrix} \right]$. Reflection across the $x$-axis: $\left[ \begin{matrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{matrix} \right]$. Dilation by $k$: $\left[ \begin{matrix} k & 0 \\ 0 & k \end{matrix} \right]$.
Areas are multiplied by $\left| \det \right|$; a negative determinant reverses orientation.

misconception.right: The images go in as columns, not rows: the matrix is $\left[ \begin{matrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{matrix} \right]$. Check: it sends $\left\langle 1, 0 \right\rangle$ to its first column, $\left\langle 2, 1 \right\rangle$.

summary: A linear transformation sends $\left\langle x, y \right\rangle$ to $\left\langle ax + by, cx + dy \right\rangle$, which is the matrix $\left[ \begin{matrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{matrix} \right]$ times the input. Its columns are the images of $\left\langle 1, 0 \right\rangle$ and $\left\langle 0, 1 \right\rangle$. Rotations, reflections, dilations and shears are all linear, and every area is multiplied by the absolute value of the determinant.
